1.title: High-Performing Network Architectures
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: High-Performing Network Architectures. This module covers task statement three point four. You will plan the address space, bring content close to users with edge services, connect networks, and choose a load balancing strategy. The exam describes a global, hybrid or multi-tier need, and asks you to pick the network design.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Plan I P addressing, subnet tiers and resource placement. Use CloudFront and Global Accelerator as edge networking services. Connect networks with peering, Transit Gateway, Private Link, V P N and Direct Connect. Pick a load balancing strategy. And build global, hybrid and multi-tier topologies that can scale.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Goes Global
1.text: Lantern and Loom is going global. Overseas shoppers see slow page loads. A partner needs fixed I P addresses to reach the order A P I. Three V P C s, for production, shared services and analytics, must talk to each other. And an office link must reach them all. Your job is to design a network that is fast and ready to grow.

1.title: IP Addressing and CIDR Planning
1.text: Start with the address plan. A V P C needs an I P version four C I D R block from slash sixteen, which is sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six addresses, down to slash twenty-eight, sixteen addresses. Use private ranges, such as ten dot zero, one seventy-two dot sixteen, and one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight. Choose ranges that do not overlap with other V P C s or with your on-premises network, because peering and Direct Connect gateways need that. You cannot resize a block, but you can add secondary C I D R blocks. Plan for growth, with subnets per zone and per tier. I P version six adds dual-stack and I P version six-only subnets. And public I P version four addresses are charged. Exam tip: overlapping ranges are the classic reason peering and hybrid links fail.

1.title: Placing Resources
1.text: Placement turns requirements into locations. For low latency for users, choose a Region near them, plus CloudFront or Global Accelerator. For high availability, use two or more Availability Zones per tier. For low latency between nodes, use a cluster placement group in one zone. For data location rules, use the Region that satisfies them. Keep private tiers in private or isolated subnets, with the load balancer in public ones. And remember that traffic inside one zone costs less than traffic across zones. Exam tip: decide users, failure size and rules first, then place Region, zone and subnet.

1.title: Amazon CloudFront
1.text: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network. It keeps copies of content at edge locations near viewers. A cache hit is answered at once. A cache miss goes to the origin, which can be S three, a load balancer, E C two, or any H T T P server. By default, content stays in the cache for twenty-four hours, and you can set T T L s per path. It serves static and dynamic content, streaming and A P I s, and you can add H T T P S, A W S W A F and Shield. The figure shows a viewer, a nearby edge cache with hit and miss paths, and the origin. Exam tip: global users and slow content points to CloudFront.

1.title: CloudFront Origins and Private Content
1.text: To keep an S three bucket private, let only CloudFront read it, using origin access control. It replaces the older origin access identity, and it supports S S E dash K M S and all Regions. Signed U R L s and signed cookies restrict who can view content. With origin failover, if the primary origin fails, CloudFront can try a secondary origin. Data transfer from A W S origins to CloudFront is free. To refresh content, invalidate it or version the file names. Exam tip: a private bucket behind CloudFront uses origin access control, not a public bucket.

1.title: Edge Compute: CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge
1.text: CloudFront can run your code at the edge in two ways. CloudFront Functions use JavaScript, start in under a millisecond, and handle millions of requests per second. Use them for header changes, redirects, U R L rewrites and simple authentication. Lambda at Edge uses Node dot J S or Python, and handles complex logic with more time and resources, such as heavier processing or calls to other services. You publish a Lambda at Edge function in one Region, and it is replicated to the edge. Exam tip: light and fast means CloudFront Functions; heavy or full application logic means Lambda at Edge.

1.title: AWS Global Accelerator
1.text: A W S Global Accelerator gives your application two static anycast I P addresses, or four with I P version six, from the A W S edge network. Traffic enters at the nearest edge and travels on the A W S global network. A standard accelerator sends users to the best healthy endpoint: an A L B, an N L B, an E C two instance, or an Elastic I P address, in one or many Regions. Health checks shift traffic at once, and traffic dials control the split. A custom routing accelerator maps a user to one specific destination. There is no D N S caching delay. Exam tip: static I P addresses plus fast regional failover for T C P or U D P means Global Accelerator.

1.title: CloudFront or Global Accelerator?
1.text: CloudFront or Global Accelerator? CloudFront caches content at the edge, and suits H T T P and H T T P S content, static and dynamic. It offers origin failover per request, and its edge addresses change. Global Accelerator routes traffic over the A W S network without caching, and suits T C P and U D P, games, voice, and A P I s that need fixed I P addresses. Its failover is health-based and near-instant, and it gives two static addresses. Route fifty-three latency routing, by contrast, picks a Region by D N S. Exam tip: cache it with CloudFront; accelerate and fail over without caching with Global Accelerator.

1.title: Connecting VPCs: Peering, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink
1.text: Three options connect networks. V P C peering is a private link between two V P C s, in the same or different accounts and Regions. It is not transitive, the C I D R blocks must not overlap, and inter-Region traffic stays on the A W S backbone. Transit Gateway is a hub that connects many V P C s and on-premises networks, through attachments and route tables, with inter-Region peering. It replaces a mesh of peerings. Private Link exposes one service to other V P C s through an endpoint. The consumer starts the connection, and overlapping C I D R blocks are fine. Exam tip: two V P C s means peering; many networks means Transit Gateway; one service, privately, means Private Link.

2.title: Hybrid and Multi-Region Topologies
2.text: For hybrid and multi-Region designs, use a hub. One Transit Gateway replaces many point-to-point peerings. V P N attachments and a Direct Connect gateway bring in the office and data centers. Separate route tables can keep spokes apart, for example production from analytics. Inter-Region peering joins hubs in other Regions. And keep C I D R ranges unique across all spokes. The figure shows a central transit gateway linked to three V P C s, an office by V P N and Direct Connect, and a second Region. Exam tip: many V P C s and sites call for a Transit Gateway hub, with unique C I D R ranges.

2.title: Load Balancing Strategy
2.text: Choose the load balancing strategy by need. H T T P and H T T P S routing by path or host is the Application Load Balancer. T C P or U D P, static I P addresses and extreme scale is the Network Load Balancer. Inline firewall appliances use the Gateway Load Balancer. Tier-to-tier traffic uses an internal load balancer. A global entry with fixed I P addresses puts Global Accelerator in front of A L B s or N L B s. And edge caching and W A F put CloudFront in front of the A L B. Spread targets across zones, and the load balancer health-checks them. Exam tip: pick the layer first, seven or four, then add edge services in front.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: High-Performing Networks
2.text: Here is what the exam asks. Which edge service: CloudFront, Global Accelerator or Route fifty-three. Which V P C connection: peering, Transit Gateway or Private Link. Which on-premises link: V P N, Direct Connect, or both. Which load balancer, and where it sits. And which address plan: C I D R size, non-overlap and I P version six. Exam tip: underline the words global, hybrid, static I P, private and many V P C s.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Goes Global
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Overseas shoppers see slow pages: CloudFront in front of S three and the A L B. The bucket must stay private: origin access control. The partner needs fixed I P addresses to the A P I: Global Accelerator, or an N L B with Elastic I P addresses. Light U R L rewrites at the edge: CloudFront Functions. Three V P C s and an office must connect: Transit Gateway with a V P N or Direct Connect attachment. Share one internal service with another account: Private Link. And overlapping C I D R blocks in two V P C s: re-plan the ranges, or use Private Link.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Plan non-overlapping C I D R blocks, tiers per zone, and placement by users and failure size. At the edge, CloudFront caches, and Global Accelerator accelerates and gives static I P addresses. To connect, use peering for two V P C s, Transit Gateway for many, and Private Link for one service. For hybrid, V P N and Direct Connect attach to the hub. And load balance at the right layer, with edge services in front.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom serves product pages and images from an Application Load Balancer and an S three bucket, and shoppers in other continents see slow loads. What should the architect add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: an Amazon CloudFront distribution with both origins. It caches content at edge locations near viewers. More instance power or larger volumes do not reduce distance.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. The S three bucket behind a CloudFront distribution must not be publicly readable, but CloudFront must still serve its objects, including S S E dash K M S encrypted ones. Which approach fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: origin access control, with a bucket policy for that distribution. It lets CloudFront sign requests to a private bucket and supports S S E dash K M S.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A partner sends T C P traffic to Lantern and Loom's order A P I from a fixed I P allow list. The company wants traffic to fail over between two Regions within seconds, without waiting for D N S caches to expire. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A W S Global Accelerator with endpoints in both Regions. It provides static anycast I P addresses and shifts traffic to healthy endpoints at once.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. Which two statements about V P C peering are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Peering is not transitive, and inter-Region peering traffic stays on the A W S global backbone. C I D R blocks must not overlap, no gateway or V P N is needed, and peering has no single point of failure.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Lantern and Loom is adding many V P C s and an office network, and does not want to maintain a full mesh of peering connections. Which service should the architect use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Transit Gateway as a central hub. It connects many V P C s and on-premises networks through attachments and route tables.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: D. Question three: A. Question four: A and C. Question five: C. In Module ten, we choose data ingestion and transformation services.
